record.paper_title: Developments, Applications and Open Problems in Fixed Point Theory
record.original_question: For each real p with 1 < p < infinity, take the classical sequence space ell^p and replace its norm by any equivalent norm. Does every such equivalent renorming of ell^p have the fixed point property, meaning that every nonempty closed bounded convex subset K has a fixed point for each nonexpansive self-map T: K -> K? In particular, does this hold for every equivalent renorming of ell^2?

evidence.quote: Another unresolved matter is: Does every equivalent renorming of l^p, where 1 < p < infinity, exhibit the FPP? This question remains unanswered even for l^2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A Banach space $(X,\|\cdot\|)$ is said to have the fixed point property (FPP) for nonexpansive mappings if, for every nonempty closed bounded convex subset $K \subseteq X$ and every map $T : K \to K$ satisfying $\|T x - T y\| \le \|x - y\|$ for all $x, y \in K$, there exists a point $x^* \in K$ with $T x^* = x^*$. Two norms $\|\cdot\|$ and $|\!|\!|\cdot|\!|\!|$ on a vector space $X$ are called equivalent if there exist constants $0 < c \le C < \infty$ such that $c\,\|x\| \le |\!|\!|x|\!|\!| \le C\,\|x\|$ for all $x \in X$. For a real number $p$ with $1 < p < \infty$, let $\ell^p$ denote the classical Banach space of $p$-summable real sequences with its usual norm.

Question: Does every equivalent renorming of $\ell^p$ (for $1 < p < \infty$) have the fixed point property for nonexpansive mappings? In particular, does every equivalent renorming of $\ell^2$ have this property?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether every equivalent renorming of $\ell^p$ (and in particular $\ell^2$) has the fixed point property for nonexpansive mappings appears to remain open. It is closely tied to the broader open problem of whether every reflexive Banach space has the FPP. Recent literature (including a 2025 survey on the FPP in reflexive Banach spaces) continues to list this as an unresolved question, and there is no known counterexample of an equivalent renorming of $\ell^p$, $1 < p < \infty$, lacking the FPP.

status_evidence.title: On the Fixed Point Property in Reflexive Banach Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: All known natural examples of reflexive Banach spaces have the FPP, and no reflexive space is currently known to lack it.
status_evidence.claim: The FPP for reflexive Banach spaces (which include all renormings of $\ell^p$, $1<p<\infty$) remains an open problem.

status_evidence.title: The Szlenk Index and the Fixed Point Property under Renorming
status_evidence.snippet: A renorming of ℓ2 is constructed in order to show the limitations of the usual techniques in studying the fixed point property.
status_evidence.claim: Research on renormings of $\ell^2$ and the FPP is ongoing, with constructions probing the limits of standard techniques.
